findings.text: blocking: the Measure paragraph states "The 532 test files that import reckon.crew.runs ran on both arms from git archive extractions", but the manifest's outside_scope records that neither full-population attempt reached a summary and only a 10-file focused population was run (base-arm-focused.log, head-arm-focused.log), so a landed evidence page claims coverage the run's own records contradict.

non-blocking: the retry thread calls _publish_watch_stream concurrently with the seat's ticker (runs.py:932) and nothing serialises _publish_watch_transitions, which mutates producer.known and producer.tick_deferred and appends to the stream, so an interleaved successful tick can append a transition twice or leave the fold's memory a step behind.

non-blocking: join_watch_sweeps joins producer.deferred_retry before _WATCH_STREAM_PRODUCERS.clear() at runs.py:2685, and the retry only exits on a registry check, so a retry still deferring cannot be joined; the caller pays the full timeout, reports the thread as a straggler, and the per-thread timeout doubles the bound per producer.

non-blocking: the head arm adds two failing ids against the base arm, and the host-load attribution in failure_attribution is supported by head-crashed-alone.log (8 passed) rather than by the arm itself, so §55's "adds no failure against a base arm" is satisfied by attribution and not by the measurement.
